ruleset.name: DevSecOps Reference Rules
ruleset.description: Custom PMD rules for Apex, written in XPath. The other custom rules are in pmd-custom-rules-markup.xml, pmd-custom-rules-metadata.xml, pmd-custom-rules-flow.xml, and, for JavaScript, pmd-custom-rules-javascript.xml. The stock PMD rules this reference adopts are in pmd-stock-rules.xml and, for JavaScript, in pmd-stock-rules-javascript.xml. Adjust priorities and suppressions to match your organisation's risk posture and coding standards.

rule.name: DeclareAccessOnMethods
rule.message: Explicitly use public/private/protected/global on Apex methods
rule.description: Every method that is not a test method must declare an explicit access modifier: instance and static methods, constructors, and the helper and setup methods of a test class. Apex treats a method without a modifier as private, so this rule changes no behaviour; it exists for readability and auditability, so that a reader or reviewer never has to know the default.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //Method[@StaticInitializer = false()][not(parent::Property)][not(parent::UserTrigger and @RealLoc = false())][ModifierNode[@Public = false() and @Private = false() and @Protected = false() and @Global = false() and @Test = false()]]

rule.name: DoNotUseWithoutSharing
rule.message: Use with sharing or inherited sharing, or document the justification for without sharing
rule.description: Flags any class declared as without sharing.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserClass/ModifierNode[@WithoutSharing=true()]

rule.name: RequireExplicitSharing
rule.message: Declare the sharing of this class: with sharing, without sharing, or inherited sharing
rule.description: Every outer class must declare its sharing. The reportInTestClasses property decides whether test classes are reported. Interfaces and enums are never checked, and an inner class without a sharing declaration takes the sharing of the class that calls it, so no declaration is needed there.

property.name: xpath
reportInTestClasses
property.description: Whether a test class without a sharing declaration is reported

rule.name: RequireInnerClassSharing
rule.message: Declare the sharing of this inner class: with sharing, without sharing, or inherited sharing
rule.description: An inner class should declare its sharing. An inner class with no declaration takes the sharing of the class that calls it, so the declaration is a recommendation and not a need: with it written, a reader knows how the class runs without tracing its callers.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: RequireOuterClassAccess
rule.message: Specify public, private, or global on outer Apex classes
rule.description: All outer Apex classes must have an explicit access modifier.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: DoNotRunAsCurrentUser
rule.message: Do not execute test methods as the running user - use a dedicated test user instead
rule.description: Tests must not run as the current user, for example System.runAs(new User(Id = UserInfo.getUserId())). The rule is deliberately over-strict: any UserInfo.getUserId() call inside a System.runAs statement is reported because this is a screening rule. Methods annotated @TestSetup are exempt.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //RunAsBlockStatement[.//MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@FullMethodName) = 'userinfo.getuserid'] and ancestor::Method/ModifierNode[count(Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'testsetup']) = 0]]

rule.name: NoSecurityEnforced
rule.message: Replace WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED with WITH USER_MODE
rule.description: WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED is not accepted in a query. WITH USER_MODE replaces it, and is stricter.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //SoqlExpression[matches(@Query, 'WITH\s+SECURITY_ENFORCED', 'i')]

rule.name: SwitchWithoutWhenElse
rule.message: Add a when else block to this switch statement, to say what happens for a value it does not name
rule.description: Every switch statement has a when else block, so that a value the switch does not name is handled on purpose. A switch with no when else is reported and does not block.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //SwitchStatement[not(ElseWhenBlock)]

rule.name: PreferSwitchOverIfElseChains
rule.message: This if statement compares one variable with ${minConditions} or more values. Use a switch statement on the variable
rule.description: An if statement whose branches compare one variable with a list of values reads as a list of cases, and a switch statement says that directly: each value is written once, in a when clause, and the variable is written once. The minConditions property sets how many comparisons make the if statement a switch, and it is 3 by default, so a test of one or two values stays an if statement. Comparisons with null are not counted. Check the change: == compares two strings without regard to case, but a when clause on a String is case-sensitive. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
minConditions
property.description: The number of comparisons of one variable that make an if statement a switch statement

rule.name: NullValueCheckBeforeEmptyCheck
rule.message: Check for null before calling isEmpty() on a collection, not after
rule.description: A null check placed after an isEmpty() call on the same expression runs too late; the isEmpty() call throws first. Put the null check first.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //BooleanExpression[@Op = '&&'][*[1][descendant-or-self::MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@MethodName) = 'isempty']]][*[2][self::BooleanExpression[@Op = '!='][*[1][self::VariableExpression] and *[2][self::LiteralExpression[@LiteralType = 'NULL']]]]]

rule.name: AvoidRecordTypeInfosByName
rule.message: Look the record type up by its developer name - use getRecordTypeInfosByDeveloperName()
rule.description: getRecordTypeInfosByName() finds a record type by its label, which can be changed in Setup at any time. Find it by its developer name, which does not change, with getRecordTypeInfosByDeveloperName().

property.name: xpath
property.value: //MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@MethodName) = 'getrecordtypeinfosbyname']

rule.name: ApexDocDescriptionLength
rule.message: Write a description of at least 10 characters at the top of the ApexDoc comment
rule.description: The description of an ApexDoc comment, the text at its top or the text after a @description tag, is at least 10 characters long, counted from its first letter and including spaces, across the lines it wraps onto. A shorter one, such as a placeholder, says nothing, and is reported without blocking.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: ExceptionDocumentationRequired
rule.message: Name each exception this method throws in a @throws tag of its ApexDoc comment
rule.description: The ApexDoc comment of a method that throws an exception should name each exception type it throws in a @throws tag, so that a caller knows what to catch. An exception that the method catches itself is not counted, and a method without an ApexDoc comment is not reported. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath

rule.name: DeprecatedDocumentationRequired
rule.message: Give this deprecated element a @deprecated tag in its ApexDoc comment, with the reason and the alternative
rule.description: An element with the @Deprecated annotation has a @deprecated tag in its ApexDoc comment, and the tag has text after it. The text gives the reason for the deprecation and the recommended alternative, so that a developer who uses the element knows what to use instead. A deprecated element with no comment, with no tag, or with an empty tag is reported without blocking. An enum is not read, because PMD does not keep the comment of an enum.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: FieldNameMatchesMethodName
rule.message: Rename this field or the method that has the same name
rule.description: A field or property with the same name as a method of its class makes each harder to tell from the other where it is used. Apex names are case-insensitive, so two names that differ only in case are the same name.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //Field[lower-case(@Name) = ancestor::UserClass[1]/Method[@Constructor = false()]/lower-case(@Image)]

rule.name: FieldNameMatchesClassName
rule.message: Rename this variable - it has the same name as a class
rule.description: A field or property with the same name as the class that declares it reads as a reference to the class, and so does a local variable with the name of any class declared in the same file. Apex names are case-insensitive, so two names that differ only in case are the same name.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //Field[lower-case(@Name) = lower-case(ancestor::UserClass[1]/@SimpleName)] | //VariableDeclaration[lower-case(@Image) = (/ApexFile//UserClass/lower-case(@SimpleName))]

rule.name: AuraEnabledControllerNaming
rule.message: Rename this class - a class with @AuraEnabled methods has a name that matches ${controllerPattern}
rule.description: A top-level class with an @AuraEnabled method is called from a Lightning component, and its name says so. The controllerPattern property holds the pattern the name must match, and each organisation sets its own.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserClass[@Nested = false()][not(matches(@SimpleName, concat('^(', $controllerPattern, ')$')))][Method/ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'auraenabled']]

property.name: controllerPattern
property.description: A regular expression that the name of a class with @AuraEnabled methods must match

rule.name: TriggerNameSuffix
rule.message: End the trigger name with the suffix ${suffixes}
rule.description: A trigger's name ends with one of the suffixes in the suffixes property, compared without regard to case, so that every trigger in the org is named the same way. Each organisation sets the list to its own convention.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserTrigger[not(matches(@Image, concat('(', string-join($suffixes, '|'), ')$'), 'i'))]

property.name: suffixes
property.description: The suffixes a trigger name may end with; a name that ends with any of them passes

rule.name: NoSingleLetterVariableName
rule.message: Give this variable a name of two or more letters
rule.description: A variable with a one-letter name says nothing about what it holds, so a reader has to read the code around it to find out. A local variable, a loop variable, a parameter, a field, a property, and the variable of a catch block each have a name of two or more letters that says what the variable holds. Three names are allowed in their place: i and j as the counter of a for loop, and e as the variable of a catch block. The allowedNames property lists other one-letter names that are allowed for every kind of variable, and it is empty by default. An enum value is not a variable and is not reported. The reportInTestClasses property decides whether a test class is reported, and it is false by default.

property.name: xpath
allowedNames
property.description: Other one-letter names that are allowed for every kind of variable, compared without regard to case

property.name: reportInTestClasses
property.description: Whether a variable in a test class is reported

rule.name: PreferNullCoalescingOverTernary
rule.message: Write this null check with the null coalescing operator (??), and with the safe navigation operator (?.) for a call or a field on the value
rule.description: A ternary that only supplies a default for a null value is written with the null coalescing operator (??), with the safe navigation operator (?.) where the value is a call or a field on an object. The shorter form names the value once, and it says plainly that the value has a default. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //TernaryExpression[not(ancestor::BindExpressions)][ let $test := StandardCondition/BooleanExpression[@Op = ('==', '!=')][count(*) = 2][count(LiteralExpression[@Null = true()]) = 1], $checked := $test/*[not(self::LiteralExpression[@Null = true()])], $value := if ($test/@Op = '!=') then *[2] else *[3] return exists($checked) and ( ($checked/self::VariableExpression and $value/self::VariableExpression and lower-case($checked/@Image) = lower-case($value/@Image) and ( ($checked/EmptyReferenceExpression and $value/EmptyReferenceExpression) or ($checked/ReferenceExpression/ThisVariableExpression and $value/ReferenceExpression/ThisVariableExpression) or ($checked/ReferenceExpression[not(*)][@Image != ''] and lower-case($checked/ReferenceExpression/@Image) = lower-case($value/ReferenceExpression[not(*)]/@Image)) )) or ($checked/self::MethodCallExpression[@InputParametersSize = 0][not(*[1]/*)] and $value/self::MethodCallExpression[@InputParametersSize = 0][not(*[1]/*)] and lower-case($checked/@FullMethodName) = lower-case($value/@FullMethodName)) or ($checked/self::VariableExpression[EmptyReferenceExpression] and $value[self::MethodCallExpression or self::VariableExpression]/descendant::* [self::ReferenceExpression[not(*)] or self::VariableExpression[EmptyReferenceExpression][parent::ReferenceExpression]] [lower-case(@Image) = lower-case($checked/@Image)] [every $step in ancestor-or-self::*[. >> $value] satisfies ($step/self::ReferenceExpression and not($step/preceding-sibling::*)) or (($step/self::MethodCallExpression or $step/self::VariableExpression) and $step/parent::ReferenceExpression)]) ) ]

rule.name: PreferSafeNavigationOperator
rule.message: Replace this null check with the safe navigation operator (?.)
rule.description: An if statement that only checks an object for null, and then makes one call on it or reads one value from it, is written as one statement with the safe navigation operator (?.). The statement says the same thing without the extra block and its indentation. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //IfBlockStatement[count(../*) = 1][ let $name := StandardCondition/BooleanExpression[@Op = '!='][count(*) = 2][LiteralExpression[@Null = true()]]/VariableExpression[EmptyReferenceExpression]/lower-case(@Image), $statement := BlockStatement[count(*) = 1]/*, $use := ($statement/self::ExpressionStatement/MethodCallExpression | $statement/self::VariableDeclarationStatements[count(VariableDeclaration) = 1]/VariableDeclaration[count(*) = 2]/*[1][self::MethodCallExpression or self::VariableExpression]) return exists($name) and exists($use) and not($use/self::MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@MethodName) = 'adderror']) and exists($use/descendant::* [self::ReferenceExpression[not(*)] or self::VariableExpression[EmptyReferenceExpression][parent::ReferenceExpression]] [lower-case(@Image) = $name] [every $step in ancestor-or-self::*[. >> $use] satisfies ($step/self::ReferenceExpression and not($step/preceding-sibling::*)) or (($step/self::MethodCallExpression or $step/self::VariableExpression) and $step/parent::ReferenceExpression)]) ]

rule.name: AvoidTrivialPropertyGetters
rule.message: Replace this getter, which only returns a field, with a property
rule.description: A method named getX whose body only returns the field x is written as a property instead, such as public String x { get; private set; }. The property keeps the value and the way it is read in one declaration. A Visualforce page binds to the property with the same expression, {!x}, and code that called the method reads the property. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath

rule.name: CombineNestedIfStatements
rule.message: Join this if statement and the if statement inside it into one, with && between the conditions
rule.description: An if statement whose only statement is another if statement, when neither has an else, is written as one if statement that joins the two conditions with &&. One condition is easier to read than two levels of nesting, and the code runs in the same cases. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //IfBlockStatement[not(following-sibling::*)][BlockStatement[count(*) = 1]/IfElseBlockStatement[count(*) = 1]]

rule.name: NoUnnecessaryReturnVariables
rule.message: Return this value directly instead of storing it in a variable that is only returned
rule.description: A value that is assigned to a local variable and returned in the next statement should be returned directly. The variable adds a line to read and nothing else. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //VariableDeclarationStatements[following-sibling::*[1][self::ReturnStatement]] /VariableDeclaration[count(*) = 2] [lower-case(@Image) = ../following-sibling::*[1]/VariableExpression[not(*[not(self::EmptyReferenceExpression)])]/lower-case(@Image)] | //ExpressionStatement[following-sibling::*[1][self::ReturnStatement]] [AssignmentExpression[@Op = '=']/*[1][self::VariableExpression][not(*[not(self::EmptyReferenceExpression)])] [lower-case(@Image) = ../../following-sibling::*[1]/VariableExpression[not(*[not(self::EmptyReferenceExpression)])]/lower-case(@Image)] [lower-case(@Image) = ancestor::Method[1]//VariableDeclaration/lower-case(@Image)]]

rule.name: AvoidHardcodedIpAddressApex
rule.message: Do not hard-code an IP address - read it from configuration
rule.description: A string literal that is an IPv4 address, or a URL whose host is one, ties the code to one network address. Read the address from a Named Credential, a custom metadata record, or a custom setting.

rule.name: AvoidAbsoluteSalesforceUrl
rule.message: Do not hard-code a Salesforce URL - use a relative URL, or as a last resort build it from the org domain
rule.description: A string literal that holds the absolute URL of a Salesforce org is right in one org only, because every sandbox and every production org has a host name of its own. Use a relative URL. Where a URL has to be absolute, build it from URL.getOrgDomainUrl() as a last resort. The allowedSubdomains property holds the subdomains of salesforce.com that may be written out, and each organisation adds its own.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //LiteralExpression[@String = true()][matches(@Image, 'https?://([a-z0-9-]+\.)+((salesforce|force|visualforce|salesforce-sites|salesforce-setup|cloudforce)\.com|my\.site\.com)', 'i')][not(some $s in $allowedSubdomains satisfies matches(@Image, concat('https?://', $s, '\.salesforce\.com'), 'i'))]

property.name: allowedSubdomains
property.description: The subdomains of salesforce.com whose URLs may be written out, each as the part of the host before .salesforce.com

rule.name: AvoidMagicNumbers
rule.message: Replace this number with a constant whose name says what the number means
rule.description: A number written in the code says nothing about what it means, and when the same value is needed in two places, the two copies can drift apart. A number is declared once, as a static final constant whose name says what it means, and the code uses the constant. The allowedNumbers property lists the numbers that may be written in the code, and it holds 0, 1, and -1 by default. A list index, a loop condition, a when value of a switch statement, and a test class are not reported. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
allowedNumbers
property.description: The numbers that may be written in the code, compared as numbers, with a minus sign for a negative number

rule.name: AvoidInsecureCookies
rule.message: Create this cookie with isSecure set to true
rule.description: A cookie created with isSecure set to false is also sent over a connection that is not encrypted, where it can be read. Create every cookie with isSecure set to true.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //NewObjectExpression[lower-case(@Type) = ('cookie', 'system.cookie')][*[5][self::LiteralExpression[@LiteralType = 'FALSE']]]

rule.name: AvoidWeakCryptoAlgorithms
rule.message: Use SHA-256 or a stronger algorithm - MD5 and SHA-1 are not collision resistant
rule.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are not collision resistant, and SHA-1 is being retired for every use. Name an algorithm of the SHA-2 family for a digest, a message authentication code, or a signature.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //MethodCallExpression[matches(@FullMethodName, '^(system\.)?crypto\.(generateDigest|generateMac|sign|signWithCertificate|signXml|verify|verifyHmac|verifyWithCertificate)$', 'i')][LiteralExpression[@String = true()][matches(@Image, '^(md5|sha-?1|hmacmd5|hmacsha-?1|rsa|rsa-sha1)$', 'i')]]

rule.name: AvoidDescribeInLoops
rule.message: Move this describe call out of the loop - its result is the same on every pass
rule.description: A describe call in the body of a loop is run again on every pass. When the call does not use a variable of the loop, its result is the same each time: make the call once, before the loop.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@MethodName) = 'getdescribe' or matches(@FullMethodName, '(^|\.)(fields|fieldSets)\.getMap$', 'i')][ancestor::BlockStatement/parent::*[self::ForEachStatement or self::ForLoopStatement or self::WhileLoopStatement or self::DoLoopStatement]][not((descendant::ReferenceExpression | descendant::VariableExpression)/lower-case(@Image) = ancestor::*[self::ForEachStatement or self::ForLoopStatement or self::WhileLoopStatement or self::DoLoopStatement]//VariableDeclaration/lower-case(@Image))]

rule.name: DmlInLoopAcrossMethods
rule.message: This loop calls a method that runs DML. Collect the records in a list in the loop, and run the DML once, after the loop
rule.description: A loop that calls a method which runs DML runs that DML once on every pass, and each statement counts against the limit on DML statements in a transaction. Collect the records in the loop, and run one DML statement after it. The rule reads methods of the same file only, and it matches them by name. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: let $dmlMethods := (//Method[ .//(DmlInsertStatement | DmlUpdateStatement | DmlUpsertStatement | DmlDeleteStatement | DmlUndeleteStatement | DmlMergeStatement) or .//MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@FullMethodName) = ('database.insert', 'database.update', 'database.upsert', 'database.delete', 'database.undelete', 'database.merge')] ]/lower-case(@Image)) return //MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@MethodName) = $dmlMethods] [ancestor::BlockStatement/parent::*[self::ForEachStatement or self::ForLoopStatement or self::WhileLoopStatement or self::DoLoopStatement]]

rule.name: AvoidNonSelectiveSoqlFilter
rule.message: Do not use a negative expression or a leading wildcard in a WHERE clause. It cannot use an index, so the query is not selective and reads the whole table
rule.description: A WHERE clause with a negative filter (!=, <>, NOT, NOT IN, EXCLUDES), or with a LIKE whose pattern starts with a wildcard, cannot use an index, so the query reads every row of the object, affecting performance and failing on large data volumes. Inline SOQL is read, and so is a query written as a string, wherever the string sits.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: RegexPatternsMustBeStaticFinal
rule.message: Compile this regular expression once, into a static final Pattern, instead of on every call
rule.description: Pattern.compile() and Pattern.matches() compile their regular expression each time they run, and that costs CPU time on every call. A regular expression that is written in the code is compiled once, into a static final Pattern, and the code uses that Pattern. The field also gives the expression a name, and every use of it reads the same definition. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@FullMethodName) = ('pattern.compile', 'pattern.matches', 'system.pattern.compile', 'system.pattern.matches')] [*[2][self::LiteralExpression[@String = true()]]] [not(ancestor::FieldDeclarationStatements[ModifierNode[@Static = true() and @Final = true()]])] [not(ancestor::AssignmentExpression[ancestor::Method[1][@StaticInitializer = true()]]/*[1][self::VariableExpression[not(ReferenceExpression[@Image != ''])]]/lower-case(@Image) = ancestor::UserClass[1]/FieldDeclarationStatements[ModifierNode[@Static = true() and @Final = true()]]/FieldDeclaration/lower-case(@Name))]

rule.name: NoMethodsInTriggers
rule.message: Move this method out of the trigger and into a handler class
rule.description: A trigger must not declare methods, with or without an access modifier. Logic belongs in a handler class, where it can be called, tested, and governed like any other code.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserTrigger/Method[@RealLoc = true()]

rule.name: RequireTestForOrCritical
rule.message: Add testFor or critical=true to the IsTest annotation of this test class
rule.description: A test class names the classes and triggers it tests in the testFor parameter of its IsTest annotation, or is marked with critical=true.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserClass[@Nested = false()] [ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest']] [Method[ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest'] or ModifierNode[@Test = true()]]] [not(ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest']/AnnotationParameter[ (lower-case(@Name) = 'testfor' and string-length(@Value) > 0) or (lower-case(@Name) = 'critical' and lower-case(@Value) = 'true') ])]

rule.name: TestClassIsParallel
rule.message: State IsParallel in the IsTest annotation of this test class: true if it can run in parallel, false if it cannot
rule.description: A test class states whether it can run in parallel, with IsParallel=true or IsParallel=false in its IsTest annotation. IsParallel=true runs the class in parallel even when parallel Apex testing is disabled for the org. A class that cannot run in parallel is not reported: one with SeeAllData=true, one that calls Test.getStandardPricebookId(), System.schedule(), or System.enqueueJob(), and one that creates a ContentNote, a User, a GroupMember, or another setup object that cannot be mixed with other sObjects in one DML transaction. Adapted from sca-extra, https://github.com/starch-uk/sca-extra (MIT licence).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //UserClass[@Nested = false()] [ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest']] [Method[ModifierNode[@Test = true()]]] [not(ModifierNode/Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest']/AnnotationParameter[lower-case(@Name) = 'isparallel'])] [not(.//Annotation[lower-case(@Name) = 'istest']/AnnotationParameter[lower-case(@Name) = 'seealldata' and lower-case(@Value) = 'true'])] [not(.//MethodCallExpression[lower-case(@FullMethodName) = ('test.getstandardpricebookid', 'system.test.getstandardpricebookid', 'system.schedule', 'system.enqueuejob')])] [not(.//(NewObjectExpression | NewKeyValueObjectExpression) [replace(lower-case(@Type), '^schema\.', '') = ('contentnote', 'user', 'groupmember', 'authsession', 'contentworkspace', 'fieldpermissions', 'forecastingshare', 'group', 'objectpermissions', 'objectterritory2assignmentrule', 'objectterritory2assignmentruleitem', 'permissionset', 'permissionsetassignment', 'queuesobject', 'ruleterritory2association', 'setupentityaccess', 'territory', 'territory2', 'territory2model', 'userpackagelicense', 'userrole', 'userterritory', 'userterritory2association')] [not(@ParameterCount = 1 and AssignmentExpression/VariableExpression[lower-case(@Image) = 'id'])])]
